channel.title: Value, Created
channel.description: Value, Created: a 32-chapter audiobook on the secret of value creation — what value is, how it is made, captured, and scaled. Hosted by Alex and Jordan. Produced by The Joy Digi.
channel.itunes:author: The Joy Digi
channel.itunes:summary: Value, Created: a 32-chapter audiobook on the secret of value creation — what value is, how it is made, captured, and scaled. Hosted by Alex and Jordan. Produced by The Joy Digi.

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 1: What 'Value' Actually Means
item.description: Alex and Jordan open the book with the diamond-water paradox: value isn't in things, it's in people. Desire, scarcity, and context decide what anything is worth — and creating value means changing something for someone.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 2: The Beholder's Eye
item.description: Alex and Jordan explore marginal utility: why the tenth pizza slice is worth less than the first, how the diamond-water paradox resolves at the margin, and why the last unit — not the total — decides every price and every decision.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 3: Two Faces — Use vs. Exchange
item.description: Alex and Jordan separate use value from exchange value — the warm coat versus the stock certificate — and show how confusing the two costs you at the pawn shop, in the market, and in business. Create use value, capture exchange value: the gap is where businesses live.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 4: Price Is Not Value
item.description: Alex and Jordan take on price: why a price is never a fact about a thing, only a rumor about one trade between two people — and how hearing the rumor without marrying it is the whole discipline of investing.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 5: Needs, Wants, and Pain
item.description: Alex and Jordan draw from the three wells value springs from — needs, wants, and pain — and show why pain is the deepest: people will pay almost anything to make it stop, right now.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 6: Every Value Starts as a Problem Solved
item.description: Alex and Jordan reduce the whole book to one sentence: every value ever created started as a problem solved. Trace any fortune back far enough and you find one person, one pain, one problem, solved — plus how to find problems worth your life.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 7: The Inputs: Time, Effort, Skill
item.description: Alex and Jordan break down the three inputs every creation costs — time, effort, and skill — and show why skill is the only one that compounds: stop selling your hours, spend your best effort on the hardest problem, and invest daily in the multiplier.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 8: Knowledge as Raw Material
item.description: Alex and Jordan dig into the strangest raw material in the economy: knowledge. It weighs nothing, costs nothing to copy, never depletes, and multiplies when you share it. How to stockpile it: write down the chalk marks, teach what you learn, and stand next to masters.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 9: Making Things People Want
item.description: Alex and Jordan on product thinking: why the best product does not win but the best fit does. The Segway built brilliantly for a want that never existed; the Pet Rock won on want alone. Watch behavior not opinions, build the smallest test, charge early, and build for the grievers.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 10: Service, by Hand
item.description: Alex and Jordan on the value that cannot be automated: human service. The Nordstrom tire return that bought forty years of trust, why the extra is the product, and how to deliver it: be present, solve the real problem, follow up.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 11: Attention Is an Asset
item.description: Alex and Jordan on the strangest scarcity in the modern economy: content is infinite, attention is not. Why attention is the real currency, how the attention economy harvests and sells it, and how to earn it without stealing it.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 12: Trust, the Invisible Ingredient
item.description: Alex and Jordan on the most valuable line item that never appears on a balance sheet: trust. Why trust is a tax or a dividend on every deal, how it compounds slowly and breaks in an afternoon, and three rules for building it: keep promises small and kept, overcorrect when you break it, and give it first.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 13: Removing Friction
item.description: One 'Register' button cost an online retailer three hundred million dollars a year — and nobody inside the company could see it. Alex and Jordan on friction: the waits, clicks, and forms standing between your customer and a fortune. The three-hundred-million-dollar button, the hundred-millisecond rule, and three rules for finding and killing friction in your own business before your competitors do.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 14: Recombination
item.description: Almost nothing new is ever truly invented — it is recombined. Alex and Jordan on the printing press, the iPhone, the Post-it note, and the cronut: why the parts for your next big thing already exist, and three rules for combining them into value. Next time: Chapter 15, Creating Isn't Enough.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 15: Creating Isn't Enough
item.description: Goodyear invented vulcanized rubber and died penniless; Kildall built the better operating system and lost to Gates. Alex and Jordan on why the market pays for capture, not creation: follow the bottleneck, and three rules for capturing what you create — own the scarce piece, get it in writing, build the business. Next time: Chapter 16, Pricing: Naming Your Worth.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 16: Pricing: Naming Your Worth
item.description: A Picasso napkin drawn in thirty seconds, priced at ten thousand francs. Your costs decide what you must charge, but the buyer's value decides what you can charge. Alex and Jordan break down cost-plus versus value-based pricing, the price-quality signal, and three rules for naming your worth without flinching. Next chapter: Scarcity and Moats. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 17: Scarcity and Moats
item.description: A chef builds the best restaurant in Chicago — and three copycats across the street kill it in three years. Creating value isn't enough; you need a moat. Alex and Jordan break down what stops competitors from eating what you built: relationships, secrets, and systems no copycat can clone overnight — plus the warning about moats that become traps. Next chapter: Systems That Run Without You. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 18: Systems That Run Without You
item.description: Two painters start the same business. One becomes the business — and when his shoulder gives out, income goes to zero in six weeks. The other writes checklists, trains crews, and takes July off. Alex and Jordan on turning effort into process: the step from having a job to owning an asset, and why the deepest moat is a business that doesn't need you standing in it. Next chapter: Brand: Trust, Stored. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 19: Brand: Trust, Stored
item.description: Why does a bottle of pills with identical ingredients cost five times more? Because a brand is trust with a memory. Alex and Jordan break down what a brand really is — promise, proof, and memory — how it compounds like interest (and collapses in reverse), and a practical index-card method for building one. Next chapter: Ownership. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 20: Ownership
item.description: In 1976, Ronald Wayne sold his 10 percent of Apple for 800 dollars. Wages pay for the past; equity is a claim on the future. Alex and Jordan on why owners keep what workers create — the risk asymmetry of equity, the four-rung ownership ladder from employee to owner, and the question that closes Part III: do you rent out your time, or own the asset? Next chapter: Trade: The First Leverage. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 21: Trade: The First Leverage
item.description: No single person on Earth knows how to make a pencil — yet pencils get made every day. That is trade: do one thing well, and trade for the rest. Alex and Jordan open Part IV on specialization, trust, and the first leverage — including the 80 percent trade test and the one rule: never trade the crown jewel. Next chapter: Money: Value, Frozen. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 22: Money: Value, Frozen
item.description: A fisherman's catch rots on the beach by sunset — value that can't survive until you need it is value you never had. Money is created value, frozen: durable, scarce, and trusted. Alex and Jordan on how cowrie, coin, and the database row each learned to hold value across time, why Rome's salt story still matters, and the freezer test for everything you own. Next chapter: Markets. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 23: Markets
item.description: The same fish sells for three shells in one village and eight in another, twenty miles apart. A market is where buyers and sellers discover, together, what something is worth. Alex and Jordan on the dawn tuna auction, why prices are messages, and how to become the market's favorite kind of seller. Next chapter: Leverage. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 24: Leverage
item.description: A farmer with a branch moves a boulder he couldn't budge with his back — leverage is doing more with less. Alex and Jordan on the four levers (capital, code, people, media), how Malcolm McLean's shipping container took freight from six dollars a ton to sixteen cents, and the weekly lever audit: cheapest lever first, never lever something broken. Next chapter: Distribution. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 25: Distribution
item.description: Betamax was the better machine — and it lost. Better value doesn't win; value that arrives wins. Alex and Jordan on why value nobody sees might as well not exist, how Penguin Books won distribution at the train platform, and the 50/50 rule: half your effort goes to getting it seen. Next chapter: Networks. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 26: Networks
item.description: A single fax machine is a paperweight. Two machines, and each one wakes up. A product's value isn't just what it does — it's who else is on it. Alex and Jordan on network effects: the flywheel, the dark-mirror trap of signal versus noise, and how to beat the cold start by building for the second user. Next chapter: Compounding. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 27: Compounding
item.description: One grain of rice on the first chess square, doubled on every square after, ends up bigger than mountains. Compounding is time turned into a multiplier. Alex and Jordan on Buffett's snowball, why humans underestimate the back half of the curve, and the three rules: start now, never interrupt, pick snowballs that don't melt. Next chapter: Give Value First. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 28: Give Value First
item.description: The most successful people are givers. So are the most unsuccessful. Adam Grant's research found givers at the very bottom and the very top — the difference isn't whether you give, it's how. Alex and Jordan on generosity as strategy: give with boundaries, give what you're good at, keep no score. Next chapter: The Reputation Flywheel. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 29: The Reputation Flywheel
item.description: Danny the plumber hasn't run an ad in eleven years — he's booked six weeks out. That's the reputation flywheel: every delivery lands with the customer and everyone they tell. Alex and Jordan on why reputation beats brand, how trust shortens the price conversation, and the three rules that keep it spinning. Next chapter: Choosing What to Build. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 30: Choosing What to Build
item.description: Two builders, two problems. One failed even though the product was good. Jordan's thesis: you don't choose your talent, but you do choose what you build. Alex and Jordan on taste as trained judgment, falling in love with problems instead of solutions, and the three questions that pick problems worth three years of mornings. Next chapter: Your Value-Creation System. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 31: Your Value-Creation System
item.description: Pieces are not a machine. A machine is pieces, assembled, in a loop, running on rhythm. Alex and Jordan assemble the book's multipliers into one personal system: intake that compounds, an engine of leverage, and a flywheel that feeds back on itself — plus the three rules that keep it running. Next chapter: Teach It. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi

item.title: Value, Created — Chapter 32: Teach It
item.description: The Kyoto carpenter's hands live on in his apprentices. Knowledge is the only asset you can give away and keep — and teaching is the final leverage, because the student becomes the teacher's teacher. Alex and Jordan close the book on why the best way to keep value is to give it away. The reason this book exists. Produced by The Joy Digi.
item.itunes:author: The Joy Digi
